problems: Cliopatria files Southern Tang land as 'Southern Wu' for 938-959: the Yang Wu ended in October 937 (Southern Tang page); the southern-tang dossier (another batch) must carry 937-959 and review the southern-wu 911 (from 938) and 947 shapes; southern-wu_947 is verdict wrong here.

Cliopatria files the Jin of Li Keyong and Li Cunxu (907-23 May 923) under 'Later Jin' 911-921 and 'Former Jin' 922-925: former-jin takes both, with new keyframes 907-923; its 924-925 years are the Later Tang's. The shared Wikidata id Q6201794 with 'jin' (Spring and Autumn Jin) is a Cliopatria error; they are different states.

Cliopatria's Southern Han includes northern Vietnam to 946 (204 of 1,185 cells); the Bach Dang page shows Southern Han held Jinghai only from October 930 to 931. The ngo-dynasty dossier (se-01) founds the Ngo in 939 out of southern-han land and should name the Jinghai circuit instead. southern-chu lacks a 951 loss of the Guilin and Wuzhou countries to southern-han.

Cliopatria end years are late for four states: Southern Han (971, not 979), Wuyue (978, not 979), Yan (913, not 921), Jingnan (963, not 969); starts are early or late: Southern Han 907 (not 911), Wuyue 907, Southern Wu 907, Jingnan 924 (not 926).

Page budgets exceeded: southern-han 7 pages (budget 5; the Five Dynasties and Ma Chu pages are shared), former-jin 5 (budget 2; the ea-04-c mirror events needed dated pages), jingnan 3 (budget 2). Several pages are stubs (Jingnan, Yan, Wuyue, Song conquest of Southern Han), hence the thin ledgers for southern-wu, yan-kingdom and jingnan.
Hezhong (former-jin) has no gazetteer place and is drawn as a coordinate disc; Cliopatria's 'Southern Wu' Wikipedia field is a disambiguation page (identity.wikipedia is 'Yang Wu').
